name: Ellmau
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village at the foot of the Wilden Kaiser, home to the famous Kaikogerl and the Bergdoktor filming location.
title: Ellmau
metaDescription: Ellmau at the foot of the Wilder Kaiser: The famous Bergdoktor village, SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser-Brixental, Hartkaiserbahn, Ellmi's Zauberwelt and Kaiserbad.
text:
Overview

Ellmau is situated at an elevation of 820 meters in the Sölllandl region in the district of Kufstein, nestled directly beneath the soaring limestone cliffs of the Wilder Kaiser massif. With approximately 2,900 residents, this vibrant village ranks among the most celebrated year-round holiday destinations in Tyrol. Rising steeply above the village is the Ellmauer Halt peak (2,344 m), contrasted to the south by the gentle alpine meadows of the Kitzbühel Alps. Internationally renowned as the filming location of the hit television series Der Bergdoktor, Ellmau serves as a direct gateway to the vast SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser – Brixental winter arena and an outstanding base for hiking and family adventures.

History

Settlement in the valley dates back to the High Middle Ages, with the village first documented around 1155 as Elmouwe in land records of the Augustinian Monastery Herrenchiemsee. The name signifies a riverside meadow overgrown with elm trees. From the sixteenth century onward, Ellmau prospered as an Imperial post station along the crucial travel corridor between Innsbruck, Salzburg, and Vienna, fostering an early tradition of alpine hospitality. The village center is dominated by the Catholic Parish Church of Saint Michael, constructed between 1740 and 1746 by the renowned Tyrolean baroque architect Jakob Singer. Its onion-domed steeple and ornate rococo ceiling frescoes by Johann Georg Hitzl define the village scape. Since 2007, Ellmau has garnered international fame as the home of Der Bergdoktor; the historic Hinterschnabel farmstead in the Faistenbichl district serves as the TV doctor's practice, attracting thousands of fans each season.

Getting There

By automobile from Germany, Ellmau is accessed completely toll- and vignette-free via motorways A8 and A93 to the Kiefersfelden border, continuing on motorway A12 to the toll-exempt exit Kufstein-Süd, followed by a twenty-minute drive along roads B173 and B178 directly into the village. From Salzburg or eastern Austria, route B178 leads via Lofer and St. Johann in Tirol. Train travelers arrive at international transport junctions Kufstein or Wörgl Hauptbahnhof, or regional station St. Johann in Tirol. Frequent VVT regional buses connect these railway hubs directly to Ellmau. In summer, the KaiserJet excursion bus provides free shuttle services between Ellmau, Going, Scheffau, and Söll for visitors holding the Wilder Kaiser guest card.

Tips

The state-of-the-art Hartkaiserbahn gondola whisks visitors up to 1,555 meters to Ellmi's Zauberwelt, an extensive 4,000-square-meter alpine nature play park featuring goblin trails and climbing areas. In winter, the interconnected SkiWelt Wilder Kaiser – Brixental unlocks over 270 kilometers of downhill slopes. Television enthusiasts will love touring the authentic Bergdoktor practice at Faistenbichl and hiking the carved wooden statue trail to the rustic Rübezahl-Alm. For wellness and aquatic fun, Kaiserbad Ellmau features indoor pools, thrilling waterslides, and outdoor saunas set against the rugged mountain backdrop. Mountaineers can base themselves at Wochenbrunner Alm or ascend to the Gruttenhütte refuge for high-alpine climbs into the Kaisergebirge.
